items.title: 13.8.2 Reaction of silver halides (AgX) with aqueous ammonia

source_refs.note: Topic 13.8.2 with Table 13.6 and Quick Check 13.4, printed pages 298-299.

blocks.text: Addition of aqueous ammonia tests the solubility of initially formed silver halide precipitates.

AgF is soluble in water so it does not form precipitate, so ammonia has no effect. Silver chloride dissolves in dilute ammonia to form diamminesilver(1) complex. The white precipitate of AgCl dissolves in dilute ammonia forming a colourless solution.
The cream-coloured precipitate of AgBr dissolves in concentrated ammonia, forming a colourless solution.
The yellow precipitate of silver iodide (AgI) does not dissolve in both dilute and concentrated ammonia, so there is no change in the presence of ammonia.
